newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatargas, Japan extend interim price deal to Sept.
newsitem.headline: Qatargas, Japan extend interim price deal to Sept.

text.p: Qatargas and Japan's Chubu Electric Power Co have agreed to extend their provisional price deal of $4.10 per million British Thermal Unit (BTU) for LNG by three months to September 30, company sources said on Wednesday.

"Senior executives of the two companies will meet in Nagoya or Tokyo after the summer holidays in September to discuss a definite mechanism to determine the regular price," said a source at Qatar Liquefied Gas Company, or Qatargas.
"In the meantime the provisional price of $4.10 per million BTU has been extended for a further three months," he added.

Chubu has signed a sales-and-purchase agreement (SPA) to take four million tonnes a year of LNG for 25 years from Qatargas. The first shipment landed at Nagoya in January. Price determination above a minimum of $3.60 per million BTU, the price guaranteed under the SPA, was left to periodical review.
The Qatargas price is linked to the oil price. It is subject to escalation and reduction based on oil market fluctuations.
In January, Qatargas and Chubu fixed an interim price of $4.10 per million BTU as oil prices peaked at $24 a barrel.

"Chubu has been asking for adjustment since the oil prices came below $20. But in the absence of a definite formula to calculate, the parties have not been able to change the interim price," said a source at Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC).
Qatargas is 65 percent owned by the state's QGPC, 10 percent each by Mobil and Total, and 7.5 percent each by Japan's Marubeni and Mitsui.
